newsitem.title: UK: Labour slumps five points in Scottish poll.
newsitem.headline: Labour slumps five points in Scottish poll.

text.p: Britain's opposition Labour Party slumped five points to 42 percent voter support and the ruling Conservatives slipped one to 19, the latest Scottish opinion poll showed on Tuesday.
Liberal Democrats jumped five to a new high of 15 percent and the Scottish National Party (SNP) were up one to 23 percent in an ICM poll published in the Scotsman newspaper on Tuesday.

The random telephone survey of 1,000 voters was carried out from April 11-13, a week after Labour leader Tony Blair outraged many Scots by likening the tax-raising powers of the party's pledged Scottish parliament to an English parish council.
If the poll findings turn into votes in the May 1 general election, Labour would win 52 of Scotland's 72 seats in parliament. SNP would win six and Liberal Democrats nine.
Conservatives would lose six of their 1992 seats to become Scotland's smallest parliamentary party with only five seats.
